transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I mean, it's mostly the voices. I keep hearing people talking about me. It usually happens when I'm in the office, like through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it's completely powered off. It's usually the board members or some of the senior staff, and they're just constantly saying I'm ruining the company, that I don't know what I'm doing. It sounds so real, so clear, that I actually catch myself answering them out loud before I realize nobody else in the room heard a thing. 

Which is just... it's exhausting. And honestly, it reminds me of this time when I was in college, before I dropped out to start my first business. I had this professor, Dr. Aris, who taught macroeconomics, and he would always mutter under his breath while he was writing on the chalkboard. You could never quite make out what he was saying, but you just knew it was something condescending. I used to sit in the second row, right by the window—it was a beautiful old brick building, actually, ivy growing all up the side of it. Sometimes I'd just watch the squirrels outside instead of paying attention. They're such busy little things, aren't they? Always preparing for something. But anyway, yeah, the board members... they're just so loud lately.
How has your mood been lately?

My mood? Um... I'm not really sure, honestly. I haven't paid much attention to how I'm feeling in that way. I suppose it's just... fine? Or maybe a little all over the place, kind of like the market right now. 

Which, actually, reminds me, we had to completely redo our Q3 projections on Tuesday because the shipping logistics are just an absolute nightmare lately. I was staring at the new spreadsheets, and somebody had highlighted all the negative variances in this awful, blinding neon green. My assistant, David, he loves green. He has this massive plant sitting right on the corner of his desk—a Monstera, I think it's called? The ones with the big natural holes in the leaves. Swiss cheese plant, that's it. I always wonder how those things survive in a corporate office with absolutely no natural light. The fluorescent bulbs in our suite just hum all day long. It's a very specific, low pitch, kind of like a refrigerator that's about to give out. I keep meaning to call building maintenance about it, but... wait, what did you ask me? Did you mean my mood about the office?
How long have you been hearing these voices?

Um, the voices from the walls and my phone... it's been about three months now. Right around the end of the second quarter. Which is always just an incredibly stressful time anyway because of the quarterly reviews. We had this massive catered lunch for the partners that week, and the catering company completely messed up the order. I specifically requested an assortment of gluten-free options because two of our main investors insist they have Celiac disease. Though, honestly, you never know these days if it's a real medical issue or just a fad diet. Everyone wants to be gluten-free or keto now. 

I actually tried keto for about a week last year, and I just felt so incredibly sluggish the whole time. You really don't realize how much you miss bread until you absolutely cannot have it. There's this little artisan bakery down the street from my condo that makes the most incredible sourdough. The crust is just perfectly crispy, and they bake it fresh every single morning. If I'm out on my balcony early enough, and the wind is blowing the right direction, I can smell it baking. The owner is this older gentleman, always has flour dusted all over his apron, and he sweeps the sidewalk out front at exactly 6:00 AM every day. He has this very rhythmic way of sweeping, just back and forth, back and forth... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought completely. What were we just talking about? Did you need to know something else about the bakery?
Have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Sleep? Um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed needing less sleep or anything like that. I usually try to get my standard hours, you know? It's just so hard to wind down sometimes. 

Actually, speaking of sleep, I bought this new mattress a few weeks ago. It's one of those memory foam ones that's supposed to adapt to your body temperature. The delivery guys had a terrible time getting it up the stairs to my condo because the elevator was out of service again. Our building manager is just completely incompetent. He wears these awful, brightly patterned ties—like, loud geometric shapes from the 90s—and he's always carrying around a clipboard, but nothing ever actually gets fixed. I saw him in the lobby yesterday arguing with the mail carrier about where the packages should be left. The mail carrier had this huge cart full of boxes, mostly from Amazon. It's amazing how much stuff people order online now, isn't it? Just boxes upon boxes. I used to love going to actual stores, walking through the aisles, feeling the fabrics if I was buying clothes. There was this boutique I loved in my twenties, right by the campus... 

Wait, I'm sorry. Did you ask me about my mattress?
Over these past three months, have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently down, depressed, or hopeless almost every day?

Down? Um, no, I don't think so. I haven't really had two weeks where I felt hopeless or anything like that. I mean, two weeks is a long time. 

Actually, speaking of two weeks, we just went through this incredibly grueling two-week external audit at the company. It was just exhausting. They set up camp in our main glass conference room, and the lead auditor—Richard, I think his name was—he had this incredibly annoying habit of clicking his pen during meetings. Just constantly. Click, click, click. It was one of those silver Parker pens. My grandfather actually used to carry a pen exactly like that. He kept it in his breast pocket every single day, even when he was just wearing a flannel shirt out to work in his garden. He grew the most amazing heirloom tomatoes. Big, lumpy, purple ones that tasted incredible with just a little bit of coarse sea salt. I tried to grow tomatoes on my condo balcony a few years ago, but the pigeons completely ruined them. Pigeons in the city are just so bold, aren't they? They don't even fly away when you walk up to them, they just waddle around and stare at you with those weird little orange eyes... 

Wait, I'm sorry. I completely lost my train of thought again. What were we just talking about? Did you ask me about the audit?

The interview also demonstrates marked tangentiality and derailment of thought processes. Affective episodes (both depressive and manic) have been explicitly screened and ruled out, confirming a primary psychotic disorder consistent with paranoid schizophrenia.
